Horizon webinar (link provided, click here to view): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bv_GcFnJGTg which was conducted late last year with over 180 registered attendees. This was great insight into what Horizon is and how it delivers monthly soil carbon insights and annual credit issuance to current and future registered projects. This is the 45 minute call that I mentioned in our meeting last week. AgriProve Project Proposal - Farm Management.pdf: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0xGw-0 which also formulates part of your tailored Carbon Project Plan. engagements.body: Hi Michelle, I hope you and Boyd are well and that the week has started well for you. I wanted to follow up on our land management strategy call from January 29th. We're making great progress with your project documentation, but I'm still waiting on a few key pieces of information before I can submit everything to our operations team. Outstanding Items: Project Name – We discussed this during our call, and you mentioned checking with Leesa about whether it should align with your grant funding. Have you had a chance to settle on a name? (Could be as simple as "Tansey Pastoral" or "Armstrong Creek", or something more creative!) Stocking Rate Details – You mentioned you have this information on hand but needed to pull it together. Specifically, I need: Current and historical stocking rates (DSE/LSU/AE per hectare) Duration of grazing periods Number of paddocks and their sizes/average size Rest and recovery periods Five-Year Farm Management History – This includes both the grazing history document and the horticultural management section (for your 19-hectare pecan orchard) Click here for the link to AgriProve Project Proposal - Farm Management.pdf: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0zt0n0 Paddock Maps – These will help us with the mapping phase and understanding the boundaries for both your grazing and horticultural areas Land Title Confirmation – You were going to double-check which title the potential pivot irrigation would fall under (once confirmed) Once I receive these details, I'll finalize the land management strategy document and submit it to Will's operations team to develop your carbon project plan with the intent to register the project. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or need clarification on any of these items. I'm here to help! On another note, our Head of Operations, Will Frecheville, is potentially available for a farm visit the week of February 23rd. This could be a great opportunity to walk through your property together, discuss your eligible activities in more detail, and answer any questions you might have. Let me know if you and Boyd would be interested and what day that week might work best for you. Looking forward to hearing from you. engagements.body: Hi Dean, Thanks for the chat— I appreciated your time and the chance to talk through what soil carbon could mean for your operation. The short version: AgriProve exists to make soil carbon work for farmers — not the other way around. Our job is to take the complexity off your plate, maximise your credits, and make sure you're partnered with a developer you can trust for the long term. We were the first to deliver soil carbon credits to Australian farmers and remain the fastest crediting developer in the market. engagements.subject: Your HORIZON Snapshot is ready – Wombinoo Station
engagements.body: Hi Dean, Thank you for your time and the information you shared with us last week. I'm pleased to share your link to click - HORIZON Snapshot for Wombinoo Station: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHDr8SZVCk/Sxk4EZNVAijjBP9TH6HLrw/view?utm_content=DAHDr8SZVCk&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=hf1f6cd7f24, which gives you a clear picture of what your property could look like as a soil carbon project. Here's what the modelling has identified: Across 25,658 hectares of Wombinoo Station, HORIZON has mapped 2,856.80 hectares of eligible area, spread across your creek corridors, riparian zones, and cultivated paddock country. That translates to an estimated potential of approximately 221,150 ACCUs over a 25-year project, structured across eight projects of roughly 400 hectares each. Your soil profile is genuinely interesting. The presence of Ferrosols and Vertosols through the eligible country is a real positive. Both soil types carry high carbon stability and productivity ratings, meaning the carbon you build into these soils is more likely to stay there. Your 711mm annual rainfall and soil depths reaching up to 1.53 metres provide the conditions that support meaningful and sustained carbon accumulation over time. The HORIZON zone map shows a property with real opportunity. Strength Zones through your western creek corridor and northern paddock country provide a solid foundation, while the Opportunity Zones alongside them indicate where refined grazing and pasture management could lift the entire property's carbon performance. This is exactly the kind of landscape that responds well to a well-designed soil carbon project. To get started, the next step is an AgriProve Project Proposal, which captures the key information needed to register your project with the Clean Energy Regulator. We handle the complexity from there: sampling design, field baseline work (our team comes to you), laboratory analysis, ERF registration, reporting, auditing, and ACCU issuance. Your role is providing property access and continuing the land management you are already doing. I have attached your HORIZON Snapshot for your review. I would love to walk you through it and answer any questions you have about the opportunity at Wombinoo Station. Below are some meeting time options so we can discuss further. Ben Payne 15-minute meeting: https://meetings-ap1.hubspot.com/ben2218/ben-payne-15-minute-meeting Please note: ACCU estimates and zone classifications in this Snapshot are indicative, derived from satellite remote sensing and predictive soil modelling. All figures are subject to refinement through field-based baseline sampling and final project design. engagements.body: Hi Dean, Good question, and one that comes up fairly regularly given the political landscape around carbon markets. Our Agreement covers this - "question posed to the Key Commercial Terms Project: What happens if there is a change of Government and how is the agreement impacted?: Short answer: A change of government doesn't automatically affect existing agreements. The ACCU scheme (ERF/Carbon Credit scheme) was started in 2011 - and has been through multiple government changes - so it is likely that it will remain, it may change form; but unlikely to be scrapped entirely. Historical context worth knowing The ACCU Scheme has survived multiple changes of government, including the Abbott Government's repeal of the carbon price in 2014 — the ERF/ACCU Scheme itself was actually introduced by that same government as a replacement. There is now broad bipartisan support for the scheme's continued operation, which reduces this risk considerably compared to a decade ago. What the agreement says The Master Terms and Conditions (attached) addresses this scenario directly in clause 13.6, which deals with changes to Relevant Law: If there is a change of Relevant Law that has the effect that the Carbon Projects will no longer be eligible to receive ACCUs or carbon credits under another comparable program, then either party may terminate the Agreement once any existing sale, transfer or payment obligations have been fulfilled. "Relevant Laws" is defined broadly in the definitions section to cover all laws relevant to the Carbon Projects, including the CFI Act, ANREU Act, and requirements of any regulatory authority. Regards, Ben Payne | Account Manager Phone: 1300 GO SOIL ( 1300 467 645 ) Mobile: 0483921562 Email: ben@agriprove.io Address: Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. engagements.subject: Your HORIZON Snapshot – Jonsson Farms -  Ravenshoe
engagements.body: Hi Dean, Thanks again for the chat today. I've put together your HORIZON Snapshot, which maps out the soil carbon potential across your 116 eligible hectares at Evelyn Central, Ravenshoe QLD. A few things stand out from the analysis that are worth highlighting. Your soils are exceptional. The entire eligible area is mapped as Ferrosol, a soil classification that rates high across water holding capacity, productivity, and carbon stability. Combined with 1,500mm of annual rainfall and soil depths running from 1.00 to 1.44 metres across the whole property, the Ravenshoe parcel has the kind of profile that performs well over a long crediting period. At a pasture rate of 6.0 ACCUs per hectare per year, the 25-year potential for this parcel sits at approximately 17,415 ACCUs as part of your broader Jonsson Farms project portfolio. That is a meaningful contribution from 116 hectares. On the economics, the baseline sampling cost for one project across 116 hectares comes to $7,984 (ex GST), with the option to defer that cost entirely and repay via 639 ACCUs generated in the first five years. Beyond that, AgriProve's 25% success fee covers all ongoing administration, sampling, reporting, and auditing for the life of the project. No further costs to you. I've attached your Snapshot document which walks through the HORIZON zone analysis, soil indicators, and full economics in detail. Also, click link here to view the HORIZON snapshot report: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHDmNjCiuo/vhs9p4dpolpc8juarQwV0Q/watch?utm_content=DAHDmNjCiuo&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h8a1021d647 Happy to walk through it together whenever suits. engagements.subject: Next steps ahead of your Land Management Strategy Call – Wombinoo Station/Jonsson Farms
engagements.body: Hi Dean, Great speaking with you today — it's exciting to see [Property Name] moving toward project registration. Ahead of our Land Management Strategy Call, I want to make sure we use the time well. There are three things that will help us hit the ground running: Paddock maps for each property — digital files are ideal, but hand-drawn maps showing clear boundary lines work just as well. These let us accurately configure your project areas before the call. Five-year farm management history: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0Hr-W0 — this is one of the most important pieces of the puzzle. To accurately model your soil carbon baseline and project what your land can sequester, we need a clear picture of how your properties have been managed over the past five years. Think stocking rates, pasture management, any significant land use changes — the more detail the better. Don't worry if it's not perfectly documented; we'll work through it together on the call. The AgriProve Project Proposal (Farm Management): https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0HrZ-0 — I've attached this document and linked it below. It's the foundation of our conversation, so the more detail you can fill in beforehand, the more productive our session will be. If you run into any questions while working through it, just send them through. Our Land Management Strategy Call runs around 45 minutes. We'll work through the project proposal together, assess your properties, and map out a clear path to registration. You'll leave with a solid understanding of what your project looks like and what comes next. If anything comes up before then, I'm easy to reach. engagements.subject: AgriProve Carbon Farming - Introduction
engagements.body: Thanks again for the chat this week, Richard. It was great to discuss with you some of the key aspects of what AgriProve: https://agriprove.io/ can provide and our role as Australia’s leading soil carbon developer. AgriProve's focus on scalability which simplifies the soil carbon journey, from implementation to earning ACCUs (carbon credits) AgriProve’s goal is to streamline access to soil carbon projects for farmers and help farmers take the guesswork out of practice changes while generating additional income. AgriProve has registered over 600+ projects with 75% share of all carbon projects in Australia and over 123,000+ ACCUs (carbon credits) issued over our journey with primary producers. We are also the first in Australia to deliver soil carbon credits to farmers in Australia. Please find below the links that will guide you through unlocking the potential of a soil carbon project: AgriProve - Information Pack 0725: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0wj_q0 AgriProve current project case studies: https://agriprove.io/casestudies AgriProve Portfolio Map - See what the closest soil carbon project is near you: https://maphub.net/danielwortmann/AgriProve-Portfolio-Australia AgriProve Eligibility Practices and Building Carbon: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-a-soil-carbon-project Lastly, a breakthrough in soil intelligence launched last week, giving farmers unprecedented visibility into soil carbon, access to annual crediting cycles and unlocking a new era of data-driven farm profitability.Horizon: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-a-soil-carbon-projectcombines satellite imagery with machine learning and 20,000+ soil samples to deliver prediction accuracy amongst the highest reported for similar landscapes, enabling verification on an annual cycle meaning credits are issued when carbon is stored. engagements.subject: Your HORIZON Snapshot — Bundaberg Sugar
engagements.body: Hi Ben, Thank you for the opportunity to assess the Bundaberg Sugar portfolio. I am pleased to share your HORIZON Snapshot, which covers the four eligible areas spanning the Burnett River corridor and coastal hinterland west and south of Bundaberg. See attached HORIZON Snapshot Report within this email and a click to view link provided here: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHEuM99fNU/6OcIF9EQ7iF8UsIp1mC0HA/watch?utm_content=DAHEuM99fNU&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h02e1f5840b Here is what the analysis shows across your grazing country: Approximately 4,770 hectares of your portfolio is estimated as grazing-eligible for a soil carbon project under the Emissions Reduction Fund. Across that area, HORIZON has identified 12 potential projects with an estimated potential of around 596,250 ACCUs over a 25-year crediting period. That is a significant long-term asset layered directly over the grazing management you are already running. Your portfolio sits within the 1,001–1,100mm annual rainfall band, one of the strongest performance categories in the ERF framework, and your soils include Kandosol and Dermosol, which offer good water holding capacity and moderate to moderate-high carbon stability. The depth profile across the portfolio is particularly encouraging, with approximately 65% of your eligible area estimated at optimal depth of greater than one metre. Two confirmed AgriProve projects are operating within 20 kilometres of your eligible project area, which gives us confidence that this climate zone and management context supports measurable carbon outcomes. We take care of the complexity from here: sampling design, baseline field work (our team comes to you), laboratory analysis, ERF registration, ongoing reporting to the Clean Energy Regulator, subsequent sampling every five years, audit coordination, and ACCU issuance. Your role is providing property access and continuing the grazing management you are already doing. engagements.subject: Re: KML of grazing areas
engagements.body: Hi Ben, Thank you for your patience while we worked through the detailed exclusion mapping for the Bundaberg Sugar portfolio. I am pleased to share your new HORIZON Snapshot, which now reflects the grazing-specific eligible areas across your four properties spanning the Burnett River corridor, coastal hinterland, and estuarine flats north and west of Bundaberg. Click to view link to the report also.: https://canva.link/uiu7nw2pywdh7gi Here is what the analysis shows: Your combined grazing-eligible area is 1,187.90 hectares across three estimated soil carbon projects, with an estimated potential of around 148,488 ACCUs over a 25-year crediting period. That is a meaningful long-term carbon asset built directly over the grazing management you are already running on this country. Your portfolio sits within the 1,001–1,100mm annual rainfall band, one of the strongest performance categories in the ERF framework. Soils across the portfolio are predominantly Sodosol, which responds well to gypsum application, one of the eligible management activities under the ERF soil carbon method. This gives your grazing country a clear and practical lever to build carbon performance over the project term. Approximately 60% of your eligible area is at optimal soil depth of greater than one metre, and pH across the portfolio ranges from 4.66 to 5.74, consistent with mildly to moderately acidic profiles that also open the door to lime application as an additional eligible activity. Two confirmed AgriProve projects are operating within 20 kilometres of the Bundaberg Sugar properties, which gives us confidence that this climate zone supports measurable carbon outcomes. On the economics, the baseline investment is straightforward at this scale: Option 1 involves a baseline sampling cost of $22,680 ex GST, with AgriProve's 25% success fee covering all ongoing project administration, sampling, auditing, and reporting across the project lifetime. Option 2 allows you to defer the full $22,680 baseline cost to be repaid from ACCUs generated within the first five years at $12.50 per ACCU, equivalent to 1,814 ACCUs. There is no upfront balance required under this option, with the 25% success fee applying as above. We take care of the complexity from here: sampling design, baseline field work (our team comes to you), laboratory analysis, ERF registration, ongoing reporting to the Clean Energy Regulator, subsequent sampling every five years, audit coordination, and ACCU issuance. Your role is providing property access and continuing the grazing management you are already doing. I would love to find a time to walk you through the snapshot and answer any questions. Would you be available for a call this week or next? We are also working quite closely with another sugar entity in Mackay that are looking are achieving very similar approaches that you are and I'll share a brief from them that might be the penny drop moment for our future interactions while we continue our discussions. Looking forward to your feedback and if you have any questions, let me know. engagements.subject: RE: KML of grazing areas
engagements.body: Hi Ben, You may have misinterpreted that one, but your concern is tottally understandable. Essentially, you can’t run a soil carbon project on a given area of land and convert that same land to environmental plantings for separate carbon credits. But you’re not locked out of environmental planting as a future avenue on different parts of their property, and the soil carbon project doesn't extinguish that optionality elsewhere on the farm. If there's any ambiguity about the eligibility of your specific land against the forest potential criteria, that's something I would flag with the project setup team to assess during the mapping and stratification process before registration. We would then get the soil carbon project mapped around the area you intended for environmental plantings and have the flexibility to move boundaries of the mapped project over the lifespan of the project. Hope this answers the question. Also, below is a brief that I have been working on with another sugarcane farm. I have applied XXXX for privacy of the client (I hope you don’t mind) that I’m also working on a project with. I thought this would be helpful for you to see. The Concept XXX farming system is built around a ~5-year cane rotation, with paddocks spending 12–18 months in fallow between cane crops. Rather than leaving fallow ground bare or under conventional management, XXXX returns those paddocks to multi-species pasture under high-density grazing, managed using E Shepherd (virtual fencing technology). The explicit goal of the pasture/fallow phase is to rebuild soil carbon before the paddock returns to cane production. Over a 25-year project period this would yield approximately 5 pasture rotations. His broader aims include: * Reducing reliance on synthetic inputs (fertiliser, chemicals) by rebuilding soil biology through the pasture phase * Incorporating robotics into the cane production phase for more precise input application * Using biodiversity monitoring robots to quantify ecosystem improvements alongside carbon * Proving the model on his own farm first, then rolling it out regionally with the data to back it up The expected carbon trajectory was discussed: carbon will increase during grazing/fallow phases and decline slightly during cropping phases, but the overall 25-year trajectory should be net positive — a "ladder" pattern where the incline outpaces the decline over time. ________________________________ Strategic Fit XXX has a strong interest in the platform play, data integration, and the suite of metrics AgriProve is building toward. This makes him not just a project opportunity but a potential proof-of-concept and regional advocate, given his connections across >5,000ha of regional cane. The opportunity is relatively small in isolation (XXXXha grazing component), but the bigger picture value lies in: * Proving the model works in a cane rotation system * Generating data that could underpin regional rollout * George's regional influence and connectivity as a pathway to scale ________________________________ Project Mechanics The registration and crediting structure needs careful sequencing given the rotation cycle: 1. Register the project while paddocks are still under cane — ideally just before the final harvest prior to entering fallow 2. Declare the project under cane so the declaration date is established 3. Baseline immediately upon entering fallow — so ACCU accumulation begins as soon as the carbon trajectory starts moving 4. Roll through each rotation — approximately every 5 years — repeating the process across the project life The key risk flagged by Will: don't baseline and then wait for fallow to begin, as you lose the benefit of capturing the full carbon increase from the start of the pasture phase. Timing the declaration right before the last cane harvest is the optimal approach. ________________________________ Next Steps A follow-up call has been scheduled for Friday April 10, The focus will be on: * Project mechanics…

engagements.subject: RE: KML of grazing areas
engagements.body: Thanks for clarifying that one. And yes, a decision we will have to make is weather to go down the road of soil carbon or do an environmental planting. The benefits for soil carbon farming is its low set up costs and comparable income to environmental plantings ACCU’s. The environmental planting benefits is that it keeps us open to the new biodiversity market opportunities for stacking. Interesting that you can have a flexible boundary built into soil carbon projects. Would that mean we could potentially establish soil carbon project and slowly reduce it over the years with tree planting? I get this could be counter intuitive as it takes time for carbon to build up in the soil. That is interesting with the cane farming. As I have been looking into stacked markets, would that allow this cane farmer to potentially stack reef credits on top of soil carbon credits under a reduced nitrogen application? Our current practice is to plant a soybean cover crop during fallow periods. Our fallow period does not last that long usually though. So if we were to pursue something similar we would have a land management practice change. Another recommendation I will be presenting to management is to pursue reduced nitrogen application for reef credits under a green collar project for our sugar cane land. This has a lot of potential for us as we have a lot of cane land sitting on major waterways that drain onto the southern great barrier reef. Could soil carbon stack on top of this under the sugar cane soil carbon idea? I guess it’s the same idea as above but just with the emphasis on generating reef credits with a side bonus of soil credits rather than the other way around. engagements.subject: Follow from Hobbs farm visit — Your HORIZON results are in for Tarcoola Cottage
engagements.body: Hi Georgie, Great to hear the farm visit was a great one with Hobbs. As mentioned on my text message to you earlier your HORIZON Snapshot for Tarcoola Cottage is ready, and the numbers are worth your attention. Click here the link to view results: https://canva.link/m727b5y640xzs8f This report was generated based purely on your physical address and will be more accurate once you have provided the lot and plan numbers of your property along with any paddock maps you can provide. As it stands, 337.54 hectares of your 418.71 ha property has come back eligible under the Emissions Reduction Fund — that's 80.6% of Tarcoola Cottage generating carbon credits through the grazing management you're already running. At 780mm annual rainfall, your property sits in a productive band for soil carbon, and the HORIZON model is showing real opportunity across your central and south-central paddocks to lift performance closer to your stronger eastern and northern country. Estimated ACCU potential: approximately 29,535 credits over 25 years. One more thing worth flagging — your soil pH is consistently reading between 4.68 and 4.94 across the entire eligible area. That's uniformly acidic, which opens the door to lime application and acid soil remediation as ERF-eligible activities alongside your carbon project. It's a conversation worth having. We handle everything: sampling design, field work (our team comes to you), lab analysis, ERF registration, regulatory reporting, subsequent sampling every five years, and ACCU issuance. I'd like to get 20 minutes with you to walk through the results and talk next steps. Are you free tomorrow or after the Easter break? engagements.body: Hi Shelley, Thank you for the opportunity to run the HORIZON analysis across Plumthorpe Pastoral. I've put together your snapshot soil carbon report and wanted to walk you through what we've found.Click to view link to the HORIZION Snapshot Report here: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHEWzxFRjI/exL61KRwGMkOXdtSu0QosQ/watch?utm_content=DAHEWzxFRjI&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=hd1d9273e29 The analysis has identified 8,929 eligible hectares across the property, representing 58.1% of Plumthorpe Pastoral's total area. At 812mm average annual rainfall, the property sits in a strong rainfall band for soil carbon, and with 23 potential projects across the eligible area, you're looking at an estimated potential of approximately 892,964 ACCUs over a 25-year crediting period. The soil mix is one of the highlights of this property. Vertosols and Dermosols across significant portions of the eligible area bring high water holding capacity, strong productivity, and good carbon stability to the project. The HORIZON depth map shows deep soil profiles, particularly across the northern block, with depths reaching up to 2.11 metres in the best areas. These are the kinds of conditions that underpin strong, measurable carbon outcomes. The HORIZON zone map tells an interesting story across Plumthorpe Pastoral. Strength Zones are established across the western and southwestern paddocks of the southern block, providing a solid carbon foundation to build from. The significant Opportunity Zone presence through the central and eastern sections of the northern block and the connecting corridor indicates real scope to lift carbon performance through targeted grazing management. This is the upside story in this property. Regionally, AgriProve has an active and growing presence across the northern slopes and New England zone. There is a credited project already operating in comparable grazing country approximately 35 to 40 kilometres northeast of Plumthorpe Pastoral, which gives us direct validation that this climatic zone and land type supports carbon credit generation. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot which covers the full analysis, carbon indicators, and the two pricing options available to you. Please have a read through the snapshot at your convenience. I'd love to find a time to walk you through it and answer any questions you have about the process or what a project would look like for Plumthorpe Pastoral. Would a call this week or early next week work for you? engagements.subject: Some common objections and responses that will help you
engagements.body: Hi Shelley, I just wanted to provide you with some common objections and responses you maty encountered with Kevin as a starting point. "I heard of a bloke who ended up owing money back on his carbon project." What they mean: Someone I trust told me this went badly for a farmer, and I don't want to be next. Response: That story almost always traces back to one of two things: either the project was run without a proponent — meaning the farmer was personally on the hook to the regulator — or the project was voluntarily wound up entirely. Neither of those things happen in an AgriProve project, and here's why. As Project Proponent, AgriProve carries the regulatory risk. If carbon stocks decline due to a bad season, measurement variability, or anything outside your control, that's our problem to manage — not yours. You don't receive a bill. You don't return credits. The obligation sits with us, not you. The only scenario where liability could shift back to you is if you deliberately breached the agreement — for example, clearing the project area or converting the land out of an agricultural system. Normal farming, including tough years, doesn't come close to that threshold. On property sale specifically — and this is where most of the scary stories originate — if a farmer ran a project without a proponent and sold the property to someone who didn't want to continue it, they were personally required to return every credit ever generated back to the regulator. That's the debt people have heard about. With AgriProve as proponent, that obligation transfers to us. It's our job to novate the agreement to the incoming landholder. And it's genuinely attractive for an incoming buyer to take on — the baseline has already been paid for, all future sampling and compliance costs are covered by us, and they're inheriting a proven income stream with no setup cost. There's also a five-year project review built in. On the anniversary of your project declaration, we assess performance together. If no carbon increases have occurred and the project isn't working for your country, you have the right to delist at no cost and with no obligations. You're not locked into a failing project. The only situation where you'd ever need to transfer credits back to AgriProve is if both parties agreed there was no viable path forward and the project needed to be fully terminated — and even then, that's our mechanism for managing our regulatory obligation, not a penalty imposed on you. "It's a scam. It's all just greenwashing." What they mean: I've been burned by schemes before and I don't trust anything with a government smell. Response:: That's the most common place people start. And honestly, it's a fair instinct — there have been poorly designed carbon schemes in the past. But this one is built differently. Every tonne of carbon has to be physically measured in your soil, verified by an independent auditor, and approved by the Clean Energy Regulator before a single credit is issued. You don't earn anything we can't prove. If the carbon isn't there, neither is the payment. Closing line: "Scams don't require us to come out and drill cores in your paddocks. The numbers either show up, or they don't — and you only get paid when they do." "I don't trust the government." What they mean: I don't want bureaucrats making decisions about my land. Response: Neither do we. The government doesn't run this project — we do. Your contract is with AgriProve, not a regulator. The Clean Energy Regulator is simply the body that issues the credits and audits the numbers, the same way the ATO processes a tax return. They're in the background. We're the ones on the ground with you for 25 years. Closing line: "You're not entering a compliance program. You're entering a revenue program — with us, not Canberra." engagements.subject: AgriProve - On Farm Visit - Monday 20/10 with Claudia Bryant
engagements.body: Hi Amanda, Thanks again for being available for a visit from our Customer Success Manager, Claudia. Claudia is our day-today contact with all of the current AgriProve soil carbon project holders and is a wealth of knowledge in the not only the soil carbon space but all things agriculture as well. I'm really thrilled that Claudia can connect with you on farm. I have briefed Claudia in at the stage of our conversations with your potential project and I'll have your tailored Soil Carbon Report to you this week. To anticipate next steps, I'd also ask if you can provide paddock maps of the property (digital or hand drawn mapping) and below is a link to the five year farm management history and grazing history that will assist us in understanding your properties history and establish current state of play. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve - On Farm Visit - Monday 20/10 with Claudia Bryant
engagements.body: Hi Amanda & Pete, Thanks for your time today. It was lovely to meet you and have a look around the farm. I will pass my notes from today onto Ben. That way we can get everything moving quickly. I checked in about a few things we discussed on farm: 1. The Forest Areas: When a forest area is cleared it needs to have 5 years since the clearing to be eligible for a project. This means that the area near the really scrubby bit in the corner would be best not to include. If you really wanted to 5 years after the clearing you could add it in , but that area would need to be baselined so likely wouldn't be worth it for the small area you'll gain. For the area up the top with thinner pines- that is thin enough that it isn't considered forest, so thinning those out as part of management would be okay ( if its within local NRM rule), but it would just be best to check with us before you do it so we can record it once your project starts. Question: Do you know when the pines were removed from that paddock you one way plowed was? And was it thin like the top or a thicker forest area that was cleared? 2. Selling of the Farm I was wrong about the ACCU's. They are tied to you not the land, so if you wanted to sell the farm you would be able to take your ACCU's with you. If they wanted to continue the project: they would then take over the project, we could change the activities to suit them as it would be different to before baseline, and then any ACCU's on top of what you were already issued would be theirs ( as that is what was gained since they owned it). It's very easy if they take over and it is nice and flexible to be able to farm how they want to after you have left. If they didn't want to continue the project there is 2 paths. 1. IF they are still using the land for farming and are happy for us to still come out and do the sampling every 5 years: we would report that the project was no longer continuing, still sample every 5 years to tick the box needed, but the project would be over in that they wouldn't be doing the activities or be eligible to get ACCU's even if they measured an increase in our regulatory sampling. This means you could take your ACCU's and there would be no consequence to you or them as the project would be theirs - they are just not continuing and are meeting sample requirements to still not void the contract and repayment be needed. 2. If though they were planning to NOT farm it e.g. change the land use to something that isnt farming OR they weren't happy for us to continue with the sampling- this project would need to be revoked which would require a repayment of ACCU's. This would mean repaying not just the 75% you got but also our 25% - as that is our payment and you would have to find the other 25% to pay back the government. I know that sounds dramatic, but they would only have to agree to let us take samples 1 day every 5 years ( no real work for them) for it to go with path 1 in that no repayment was required. Also, you could work this out in the conditions of the sale. E.g. If a company was buying it to change it away from farming or they really were being difficult and wouldn't let us come out for 1 day every 5 years, you could work out in the sale contract who would pay that out. That was a lot of information, so if you need me to clarify anything feel free to give me a call. I will get Ben to start organizing the next steps today, Thanks, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Brian, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. engagements.subject: Following up on our conversation yesterday
engagements.body: HI Brian, Thanks for your time on the phone yesterday, I want to ensure that I can provide the clarity and transparency you raised in our call. The use of "may" in the agreement is there to provide flexibility to adapt internal process or actions as the project develops in practice, rather than committing to a process that may not suit the conditions on the ground. It is not there to show a lack of commitment or be uncertain for what we deliver. It also reflects something that is true of soil carbon broadly: we cannot provide guarantee on what any project will return, and we won't claim that we can. What the agreement does commit to unconditionally are the services we deliver: All soil sampling after baseline (you only pay for the initial baseline sampling) Project design and onboarding Soil results analysis and presentation, including all Method calculations Registration, monitoring, reporting and audit management ACCU issuance and distribution to you If there are specific clauses that still read as uncommitted, please flag them and we'll walk through each one directly. This is a shared model. Your risk is the upfront cost of baseline sampling, and the commitment to make improvements to your farming operation for soil carbon purposes — with no guarantee those activities will produce ACCUs that offset that cost. From that point, the risk sits with AgriProve. We operate on a success fee — if no credits are generated, we don't get paid. All costs, both time and financial, for reporting, sampling coordination, project design, monitoring and measurement across the first five-year period are borne by us. We also manage the relationship with the Clean Energy Regulator, including the responsibility to relinquish credits if requested. The only circumstance in which that obligation can be passed back to you is if you have materially breached the agreement. This carries through for the life of the project, whereby we will commit to completing the work and if there are no ACCUs we do not get paid. The 25-year term is a requirement of the ACCU scheme — it applies to every registered project, not just AgriProve's. There are genuine exit points along the way. Prior to ACCUs being awarded to your project, you can elect to discontinue at any time and for any reason. If you exit within that five-year window, the only cost is that the baseline sampling cannot be recovered through the scheme. There is no further obligation to AgriProve or the Clean Energy Regulator. We provide annual reports and assessments leading into the five-year review so there are no surprises — you'll have a clear picture of whether your project is tracking well before that decision point arrives. There are additional options once ACCUs have been issued, that we can walk through should this be of concern. Lastly, Government concerns. This is a fair and legitimate concern. The straightforward answer is that no one can guarantee what any government does over a 25-year period. What we can tell you is that a registered soil carbon project sits inside a legal framework that creates real barriers to retrospective change. Your project, once registered, is a legally binding contract with the Clean Energy Regulator and Australian Government. Any material change to the scheme would carry significant legal and financial implications for the government, which is why historically, changes to the ACCU scheme have applied to projects registered going forward, not to projects already registered. Our agreement also contains force majeure provisions that apply in the event of a material change to the relevant law, meaning if the scheme were changed in a way that fundamentally affected your project, there are provisions to exit the project. Beyond the legal framework, the ACCU scheme now has substantial institutional and corporate investment behind it. engagements.body: Hi Amanda and Pete, Thank you for working through the connectivity challenges the other week - we appreciate your patience and have reviewed the full recording to ensure we captured everything discussed (see attached) Key Outcomes from Our Discussion: 1. Financial Penalty Protection - Complete Peace of Mind Your land development activities (pine clearing and cropping conversion in the back paddock) will not result in any financial penalties. AgriProve accepts the risk of carbon stock fluctuations during these remediation activities. This is clearly documented in your land management strategy, and we're fully aligned with your approach. 2. Project Structure - Two Separate Projects You've confirmed preference for two projects, which offers the financial advantage of earlier ACCU generation: Grazing Project: Improved pasture establishment (digit + legume mix) Cropping Project: Fertilizer application This structure means whichever project shows carbon sequestration first will start generating ACCUs - potentially 1-2 years earlier than a combined project. 3. Eligible Activities Confirmed Improved pasture: Digit planted November, legume mix spread following March Fertilizer application: Tracked through existing agronomist records Grazing management remains available to add later if tracking becomes easier 4. Project Area Refinement We'll remove the narrow spurs and ridge line fingers from the project map to focus on areas you can practically manage with machinery. Small rock shelves encountered during development can be addressed through sampling adjustments - this won't impact the project. Within the main paddock areas, if you run equipment over land and encounter unexpected obstacles, we can either: Remove those specific areas during sampling Use grazing as the covering activity for irregular sections 5. Understanding Project Risks The only scenario requiring ACCU repayment would be if you chose to completely change land use (e.g., residential development) after ACCUs were issued. Your planned farming activities - including potential feedlot construction - can be accommodated by excluding specific areas from the project. There's no guarantee of carbon sequestration rates, but your multi-activity approach (pasture improvement + fertilizer) positions you well for success. 6. Activity Timeline - Flexible Approach You can develop improved pasture areas progressively over the 25-year project period. The requirement is simply that eligible activities cover the project area - this could be 50% improved pasture + 50% fertilizer application, for example. Once pasture is established, you maintain it rather than re-establishing annually. Lastly, are we able to get a quick picture of the areas that you want to exclude from the current project map? A quick screenshot with areas to cut out to speed up our operations process (rather than us assuming?) Thanks again and if you have any questions, please don't hesitate to let me know. engagements.body: Hi Ben Thanks for your call yesterday, apologies I was sleeping off night shift and probably sounded as such! We have got back home now after a fairly ordinary month of being away. With a death in the family comes change- change which we certainly were not foreseeing anywhere on our radar any time soon. Now that Mum is gone, Dad is unsure of his future on their property alone as he also ages. The next 12months will give us all a bit of time to process and think about what the future might look like and potentially put plans in place- but one highly likely scenario that is being talked about is the sale of both our property and my father’s to consolidate into one property somewhere likely in QLD where we can continue our business ventures but also look after Dad living on the same property as he ages and maintains involvement in agriculture for as long as he is physically able to. Therefore, I think it would be unwise for us to move ahead any further with signing up to a soil carbon project at this stage when our property may be going on the market before ticking the boxes for the eligible activities being done. I know we have put a lot of work into the back and forth of trying to understand the carbon concepts and especially get the mapping side correct; and I am not saying it is off the table forever as it is something we are very much interested in proceeding with; however given the change in direction of our family I think we should just pause now and let some time go by until decisions are made. engagements.subject: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project - Introduction
engagements.body: Hi Dan, Thanks again for the chat earlier. I wanted to ensure you have as much information and support from AgriProve as possible. AgriProve is Australia’s leading soil carbon developer with a focus on scalability and farmer-led solutions which simplifies the soil carbon journey, from implementation to earning ACCUs (carbon credits) As mentioned, we can provide some preliminary mapping with our lot and plan numbers which are accessible from any current rate notices you have. AgriProve’s goal is to streamline access to soil carbon projects for farmers, and help farmers take the guesswork out of practice changes. Attached is a developer checklist is for your assistance as well. AgriProve has registered over 550+ projects with 75% share of all carbon projects in Australia and over 180,000 hectares under management. We are the first in Australia to deliver soil carbon credits to primary producers. AgriProve currently have over 80,000 ACCU’s issued along with a further 190,000 under crediting which is growing every day. We are also the fastest crediting soil carbon developer in the market. Please find below the links that will guide you through unlocking the potential of a soil carbon project: AgriProve - Information Pack 0725: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0hgRq0 AgriProve current project case studies: https://agriprove.io/casestudies AgriProve Portfolio Map - See what the closest soil carbon project is near you: https://maphub.net/danielwortmann/AgriProve-Portfolio-Australia AgriProve YouTube Archive - Past webinars, videos, advice and more: https://www.youtube.com/@agriprove/videos AgriProve’s FREE platform provides farmers with a cutting-edge, science-based solution for managing their environmental impact and improving farm productivity. By seamlessly integrating soil carbon project assessments with emissions intensity evaluations, our platform empowers farmers to make informed decisions about land management. Below is a link to creating a free account: AgriProve Tutorial Video to creating a free account: https://www.loom.com/share/bb04b2e0d2164ce0bef5a47b46826cd3?sid=092be4b5-e496-485c-b53a-1e491eeee6dd Link to create a free account on the AgriProve platform: https://agriprove.io/casestudies If you have any initial questions, please let me know and looking forward to speaking to you on Friday. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project - Introduction
engagements.body: Hi Dan, Thank you for the opportunity to run the HORIZON analysis across your additional Home Block at Mount Tom. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot (click to link provided also: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHDmHbkPQM/gMKzVnM4uZDs8TLtPfjNIg/watch?utm_content=DAHDmHbkPQM&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f6ce7bb8f), and wanted to walk you through what it shows and what it means for your property. What the analysis found: HORIZON has identified 142.94 hectares of eligible land across your 305.49 ha property, sitting within the Miriam Vale coastal hinterland at 1,050mm annual rainfall. At that rainfall level, your land falls into our highest ACCU rate tier, with an estimated potential of 5.0 credits per hectare per year. Over a 25-year crediting period, that points to an estimated 17,868 ACCUs gross from this block. The zone map shows a mixed picture across your eligible area, with Strength Zones concentrated along the western fringe and southern boundary, and Opportunity Zones broadly spread through the central and eastern sections. That spread tells us there is meaningful room to lift carbon performance across the property through adjusted grazing management, and your strongest country provides a solid foundation to build from. A candid note on scale: I want to be straightforward with you. At 142.94 eligible hectares, this block sits below the usual standalone threshold we typically require to register a project under the ERF soil carbon method. That is not a reflection of your land's carbon potential, which is genuine, but rather a practical constraint of project economics and regulatory design. The good news is that, with the additional land under separate title or management, those areas could be assessed and combined with this block to reach a viable project scale. In the meantime, your HORIZON Snapshot gives you something genuinely useful regardless of the project pathway. The zone maps, soil depth data, and carbon distribution analysis are a practical tool for understanding where your land is performing and where targeted management could make a difference. I would love to have a conversation about what the options look like for your situation. Would you have time for a quick call in the next week? Happy to work around what suits you. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Farm Visit with Hobbs Margaret
engagements.body: Hi Jon, Thanks for your time with Hobbs yesterday and your interest in exploring soil carbon for The Willows and your other prospective clients with your portfolio. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot, which shows the estimated opportunity based on our analysis and amended the annual rainfall as rquested. You have 749 eligible hectares across the property, with Chromosol soils that create conditions suited to carbon building under improved management. The analysis shows Strength Zones scattered across the western paddocks, through the northern sections, and across the southern and eastern blocks where modeled carbon levels currently sit above the property median, and Opportunity Zones prominent across the northern paddocks and through central sections where targeted grazing management could support carbon gains. With 650mm of rainfall and soil depths reaching 2.1m across extensive areas, there's substantial capacity for carbon storage in the soil profile. The 82% eligibility rate is strong—satellite analysis excluded forests, infrastructure, and waterways, leaving 749 hectares of project-ready grazing land across your 911-hectare property. We're projecting approximately 56,175 ACCUs over 25 years based on our rainfall band methodology. At 749 eligible hectares, Growth Farms is well-positioned for two efficiently scaled projects (~400ha each). You're situated in a highly active region—approximately 40 neighboring properties across the Wagga Wagga-Tumut corridor are at various project stages, and credited projects within 50km are actively receiving credits, demonstrating these conditions support carbon building. Next steps will be focused on a tailored Land Management Strategy Call which is approx. 45 minutes to understand the properties history, current practices and how you would like to implement improved soil health practice with the intention of undertaking a soil carbon project with AgriProve. So we can arrange baseline soil sampling prior to Autumn, it would be great to lock in a time for the Land Management Strategy Call next week. Below is a link to schedule a time for this call. 60 min, 30 min, and 15 min meeting: https://meetings-ap1.hubspot.com/ben2218 If you have any questions, let me know and I'll touch base with you before the end of the week. engagements.subject: Your HORIZON Snapshot — Hunter Valley Wagyu Weemala
engagements.body: Hi James, I hope you're well. I'm pleased to share your HORIZON Snapshot for your first property, Weemala. I've attached the full Snapshot for your review and provided a click to the link HORIZON Snapshot here: https://canva.link/jtril8tgd6g74j6. The analysis has identified 58.77 hectares as eligible for a soil carbon project, representing 78.9% of the property. At 1,328 mm of annual rainfall, Weemala sits in our highest ACCU rate band, giving the property an estimated potential of around 8,816 ACCUs over a standard 25-year crediting period. The HORIZON map reveals a strong base of carbon performance across the western and central-western paddocks, with meaningful Opportunity Zones through the eastern and southern areas where targeted grazing management could lift performance further. There is also a notable soil health story at Weemala. The pH data shows strongly acidic conditions across the full eligible area (4.53 to 4.76), and lime application and acid soil remediation are both eligible activities under the ERF. This opens a practical conversation about layering soil health improvement alongside the carbon project, with the costs of those activities potentially supported through the program. As mentioned in our previous conversations, at 58.77 eligible hectares, Weemala sits below the standalone project registration threshold under the ERF. On its own, the property isn't quite large enough to register as an independent project. The good news is that this is a straightforward pathway to resolve, and one we work through with landholders regularly. Combined eligible area across your other properties brings the project to the required scale, and Weemala's high-rainfall, high-rate contribution becomes a meaningful part of a larger, commercially viable whole. engagements.subject: Riverina soils might be worth more than you think
engagements.body: G'Day James, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural "carbon sink" where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years. Why This Matters for Carbon: The combination of your soil types, pH management and yearly rainfall combination generate a significant carbon opportunity If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? engagements.body: Hi James, Thanks for your interest in exploring soil carbon at Currajong. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot, which shows what the property looks like through a carbon lens. The link to HORIZON Snapshot is provided (click link here): https://www.canva.com/design/DAG_rXPE1Jg/-Um5rKmktqZwZPNFksFa4A/view?utm_content=DAG_rXPE1Jg&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h25e0d4e25falso. Currajong has got 1,946 eligible hectares across the property, with Chromosols (83%) and Sodosols (17%) that provide a reliable foundation for your mixed grazing and cropping enterprise. The analysis shows clear Strength Zones prominently across the western and central-western paddocks where carbon is already performing well, and Opportunity Zones across the northern paddocks and dominating the southeastern block where targeted rotational grazing and improved cropping practices could lift carbon further. With 444mm of rainfall and approximately 35% of the property showing optimal soil depth over 1 meter, there's genuine capacity to build carbon here. You're in good company—we're seeing growing momentum across the Riverina, with approximately 35 properties within 150km exploring soil carbon opportunities, and multiple properties already measuring gains. The nearest credited project is about 80km to the east-northeast, demonstrating that the fundamentals work in this region. Across 1,946 eligible hectares, we're estimating around 82,700 ACCUs over 25 years. The scale is right, and we'd be keen to explore what a partnership could look like for Currajong's mixed enterprise. Let me know if you'd like to jump on a call to talk it through on Monday. I thought I’d send a bit of context ahead of the call on what George Williams is doing on his Dawlish Road place at Sarina, which I’ve been helping him with. He’s been trialling an enhanced fallow approach within his cane rotation — basically taking that ~15–20% fallow area and planting it out to forage (ryegrass / sorghum), then grazing it with cattle. The idea is pretty simple — turn the fallow phase from something that’s just sitting there into a productive and biologically active part of the system, without interfering with the cane program. From what we’re seeing (and from similar setups), it’s doing a good job on: groundcover and soil condition moisture retention and structure and importantly, follow-on crop performance In a few comparable cases, growers are talking about 30–50% lift in the next plant cane, which is pretty interesting. From our side, another layer to it is that it ties in neatly with Paniri’s weaner program — particularly cattle coming down from the Cape. The fallow effectively becomes a distributed backgrounding system, and with eShepherd we can run cattle across unfenced areas and manage grazing properly without needing to build infrastructure. Where I thought this might be relevant to you is around the measurement side of things. Because it sits within a ~5-year rotation, it gives us a pretty clean opportunity to: set a baseline going into fallow monitor what happens through the grazing phase then track what flows through into the next cane crop Timing-wise, we’re looking to start the trial properly in June, once the cane is removed from the areas going into fallow. That gives us a good opportunity to set a baseline and structure things properly from the outset. We’re not assuming there’s a carbon outcome here, but it felt like something worth running past you to see whether: there’s a credible way to measure this properly, and whether there might be a carbon angle over time (soil, fertiliser reduction, etc.) At a bigger picture level, if something like this stacked up, there’s a fair bit of scale sitting behind it with cane — but probably best to walk through that together.

engagements.subject: Re: Soil Carbon Proposal Plan - Update
engagements.body: Hi Dan, I hope you're well. As an FYI - we will be likely moving to a more regular position where all of our landholders and partners will be required to have their own ANREU account to hold their ACCUs (this is the same set up Adam Gunthorpe has for his ACCU's essentially) Setting up an ANREU account can be done via the CER's website; or we can do it on behalf of the landholder once your Key Commercial Terms have bene signed. https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance What this means, is we have a number of marking positives and offerings that can be put to the landholder. We can absolutely set up an ANREU account for you Landholder has full flexibility and autonomy of their ACCUs You can elect to sell either through AgriProve or on their own, or through another broker This avoids a brokerage fee or holding fee from AgriProve if they have their ACCUs transferred and broker through someone else. We will look for formalise a process for setting up these accounts, starting with our landholders who have already been issued credits, and then working through clients with a measured increase and then onto clients as a part of their onboarding/re-sampling. engagements.subject: Your HORIZON Snapshot — Lilymere Agriculture
engagements.body: Hi Erin, Thank you for your interest in AgriProve's soil carbon project. I'm pleased to share your HORIZON Snapshot for Lilymere Agriculture click here to view link: https://canva.link/fm2bfew0a918cnt, which gives you a detailed picture of your property's soil carbon profile and the opportunity it holds. Our HORIZON model has mapped 67.70 hectares of eligible area across your Glen William property, representing 56.8% of your land. The analysis shows a strong soil depth profile across the eligible area, ranging from 0.63 to 2.10 metres with no shallow or constrained country, which is a positive indicator for carbon sequestration potential. At 850mm annual rainfall, your property sits in AgriProve's 4.0 ACCU per hectare per year estimation band. Over a standard 25-year crediting period, your eligible area could support the generation of approximately 6,770 ACCUs. Your Kurosol soils carry moderate water holding capacity and carbon stability, and the depth and rainfall combination provides a genuine foundation to build from. One thing worth discussing when we connect is your soil pH. The HORIZON data shows your eligible area is running at pH 4.47–4.64 across the board, which sits in the strongly acidic range. Lime application to remediate acid soils is an ERF-eligible project activity, so there's a practical conversation to be had about how a carbon project can complement soil health improvements you may already be considering. AgriProve has active and credited projects operating across the Hunter Valley corridor, including a credited project approximately 8–10km to the northwest. This region has a demonstrated track record for measuring and generating verified soil carbon credits, and Lilymere Agriculture is well-positioned within that context. The attached HORIZON Snapshot outlines everything relevant to a potential soil carbon project. Beyond the baseline, AgriProve handles everything: sampling design, field work (our team comes to you), laboratory analysis, ERF registration, Clean Energy Regulator reporting, subsequent sampling every five years, audit coordination, and ACCU issuance. Your role is providing property access and continuing the land management you're already doing. I look forward to seeing you this Friday to go through the Snapshot and answer any questions you have. engagements.subject: AgriProve - A soil carbon conversation worth having
engagements.body: Hi Erin, Great connecting with you the other week. As discussed, amongst many other things, AgriProve exists to make soil carbon work for farmers — not the other way around. We handle the complexity, maximise your credits, and stay with you for the long term. The numbers back it up: 650+ registered projects, 75%+ market share of Australian soil carbon projects, and 139,000+ ACCUs issued to primary producers. We were the first to deliver soil carbon credits to Australian farmers and remain the fastest crediting developer in the country. What that means for your operation: → A project designed around your farming system → Annual crediting through our HORIZON platform — no five-year wait → Full transparency on your ACCU account and credit delivery → A dedicated specialist with you from eligibility through to income: A few resources to explore in your own time (click to view below links) Information Pack: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0PqHk0 Case Studies: https://agriprove.io/casestudies Portfolio Map: https://maphub.net/danielwortmann/AgriProve-Portfolio-Australia Eligible Practices: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-a-soil-carbon-project Master T's & C's: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0PqG30 Lastly— AgriProve has just formalised a partnership with Verterra that's going to open up some genuinely exciting possibilities for landholders down the track. The idea is to stack soil carbon with other natural capital projects on the same property — things like water quality credits, environmental planting, and biodiversity — so the land is working harder across multiple income streams at once. It's still early days and we're working through the methodology and pilot program details, but the commercial framework is in place and this is very much where AgriProve is heading nationally. For a property like yours, it's worth keeping in mind as we progress the soil carbon side of things. Happy to answer any questions or jump on a call when the timing suits. engagements.subject: Riverina soils might be worth more than you think
engagements.body: G'Day Jamie-Lee, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural "carbon sink" where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years. Why This Matters for Carbon: The combination of your soil types, pH management and yearly rainfall combination generate a significant carbon opportunity If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? engagements.subject: Kismet Stud — your HORIZON results are worth a conversation
engagements.body: Hi Graham and Carly, I hope this finds you well. I wanted to reach out and share something we've put together specifically for Kismet Stud. We've run your property through HORIZON, our satellite-based soil carbon modelling platform, and the results are genuinely encouraging. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot, which gives you a detailed picture of what a soil carbon project could look like across your land near Howlong. Here's what the analysis shows: Kismet Stud carries 406.79 eligible hectares, representing approximately 94.5% of your total property. Your dominant Chromosol soils, combined with 545mm of annual rainfall, present conditions that align well with credible carbon sequestration. Strength Zones are concentrated across the central and northern portions of the property, indicating where conditions are modelled as most favourable. The HORIZON model estimates a potential of approximately 30,509 ACCUs over a 25-year crediting period, at a rate of 3 ACCUs per hectare per year. To put that in regional context, six AgriProve projects are already active within 50 kilometres of Kismet Stud. engagements.subject: Restrictions realting to irrigation for your carbon projects:
engagements.body: Hi Jason, Thanks again for today. A summary of the issues relating to irrigation for your carbon projects: Irrigation is a restricted activity under s.12(8) of the Methodology After completion of the baseline sampling round, irrigation may be applied to CEAs (Carbon Estimation Areas) within a project area only if both of the following apply: disregarding new irrigation, the annual level of irrigation for the project area is not more than 20% greater than the highest annual level of irrigation in the baseline period; disregarding new irrigation, the 5-yearly total level of irrigation for the project area is not more than 20% greater than the total level of irrigation in the baseline period. For example, if there was 10ML of irrigation applied in 2020, 5ML of irrigation in 2021 and none during the other baseline years, the project/CEA is restricted to: Using no more than 12ML of irrigation in any 1 year, and Using no more than 18ML in a 5-year period. 'New irrigation' is defined as “new or additional irrigation applied to land in a project area using water obtained through irrigation efficiency savings made after the date on which the section 27 declaration of the project was made” and is a result of improving the efficiency of irrigated water through one or both of the following: (i) on-farm irrigation infrastructure located within the project area; (ii) management practices within the project area This means that ‘new irrigation’ is essentially a redistribution of irrigation derived from efficiency savings, not simply applying more water. There is no restriction on how the water is redistributed, for example to other parts of the CEA under new irrigation infrastructure, so long as the water is derived from those efficiency savings. Hope that adresses your question and let me know if you have any others. engagements.body: Hi Paul, It was great reconnecting with you and sorry it's taken a few weeks to come back to you. I've put together your new HORIZON Snapshot for Paul Webster Pastoral, which I've attached to this email.Also a clickable link provided here: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHE6CcLLbM/GCwGoCchg3wNE2uh9dg7JQ/watch?utm_content=DAHE6CcLLbM&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h2120de5500. The analysis covers both properties and identifies approximately 360 hectares of eligible area across the properties, representing 63% of your total land. HORIZON has mapped how carbon is currently distributed across your landscape, giving us a clear picture of where your stronger country sits and where the most significant opportunity lies. A few things worth highlighting from the analysis: Your southern property shows genuine Strength Zone presence through its central and eastern sections, indicating carbon levels above your property median. This is encouraging. The northern property is dominated by Opportunity Zones, which reflects where targeted grazing management has the most capacity to lift carbon performance over time. Your soils are Dermosol and Sodosol across the eligible area, with a rainfall average of 725mm. At an estimated rate of 3.5 ACCUs per hectare per year, the property has a projected potential of approximately 31,479 ACCUs over a 25-year crediting period. Baseline sampling is estimated at $7,984 ex GST, with the option to defer that cost entirely against future ACCUs if preferred. One thing I want to be upfront with you about: at 360 eligible hectares, the property sits just slightly below the 400 hectare threshold for standalone project registration under the ERF. This means participation would be via AgriProve's aggregation pathway, where we group eligible properties together to meet registration requirements. It's a well-established route, and many of our clients across Victoria participate this way. It doesn't change the ACCU potential or the economics for you as a landholder. I'd love to walk you through the snapshot and answer any questions you have about what the aggregation pathway looks like in practice. Would you have 20 minutes for a call this week or next? Looking forward to hearing your thoughts. engagements.subject: AgriProve Carbon Farming - Introduction
engagements.body: Hi Leon, I hope you're having a great week. I'm Ben from AgriProve: https://agriprove.io/, Australia's leading soil carbon project developer. Pieter from mOOvement, who AgriProve have recently partnered with, has shared your interest in a potential soil carbon project AgriProve: https://agriprove.io/ has registered over 600 projects nationally and delivered the country's first soil carbon credits to farmers. We specialise in making soil carbon projects simple. Here's how it works: We analyze your property to understand how much carbon your soils can sequester We work with you to develop a management plan that builds soil carbon while improving productivity You maintain full control of your land management — we handle all the regulatory complexity and compliance What makes us different: With 25,000 soil samples in our database, we've built Australia's largest soil carbon knowledge base. This means we can provide insights specific to your region, soil type, and production system — backed by real data from farms like yours. Interested in exploring your property's potential? engagements.body: Hi Georgie, Thank you for taking the time to come back to me — I really do appreciate the transparency, and I completely understand the position you're in. Before we close the door, I'd love the chance to have a quick conversation, because flexibility around property titles is something we can work with. We're able to design projects around specific areas of the holding, and if the smaller block is the concern, there may well be a way to structure things that keeps your options open for when the time comes. We have a Key Commercial Terms catch-up this Friday that would be a perfect opportunity to walk through this together — it's relaxed, no pressure, and I think even thirty minutes could give you a much clearer picture of what's actually possible. Would you be open to continue with our video call Friday? I'd hate for a concern we might be able to solve to be the thing that ends the conversation. Warm regards, Ben Hi Ben, After going over the documents and much discussion with other family members, unfortunately we are unable to proceed with the project. You see, we are thinking of selling off the smaller title somewhere in the near future and the project will not allow for this. So, it is not the project that is the issue, but the short-term flexibility we need for our move towards retirement, I'm sure you understand our predicament. It was great to meet Hobbs and yourself. Regards Georgie Millard ________________________________ From: Ben Payne Sent: Thursday, 30 April 2026 1:52 PM To: William Cottrell Subject: Ben Payne sent you 2026-04-24 - AgriProve Agreement + Key Commercial Terms - Tarcoola Carbon Project - Cottrell Ben Payne sent you 2026-04-24 - AgriProve Agreement + Key Commercial Terms - Tarcoola Carbon Project - Cottrell. Hi Georgie and Will, Attached is a copy of our Key Commercial Terms for your review via our eSignature provider - PandaDoc. This document, alongside our included Master Terms and Conditions, comprises our full Sales and License agreement for your Carbon Project(s). Click 'Open Document' to view the document. There are then two options to sign it: 1. Electronically (e)Sign the document. When you are ready to complete and sign the document, click 'Start' when the document has opened. It is easier if all landholders are present so you can all sign it in one go. Note that the signing order is sequential; the first recipient must complete all required fields before the document is sent to the next recipient. 2. Download the document by clicking on the three vertical dots on the top bar and select 'Download as PDF'. You can then print, physically sign, and scan back to us. The agreement also grants AgriProve the licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit the carbon project/projects for the term of the agreement. The key responsibility for you is to maintain the property in an agricultural system. Also note that as a signatory to the Carbon Industry Code of Conduct, we recommend that you seek independent legal and/or financial advice before signing the Key Commercial Terms. You can forward this document to your solicitor, accountant or other party by clicking the 'Forward' button below. Additionally we have prepared a list of commonly asked questions about the contract that you may also share with your solicitor: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Please review, and don't hesitate to contact us if you have any further questions. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve - A soil carbon conversation worth having
engagements.body: Hi Phil. I wanted to follow up and share a little more about what a soil carbon project actually means on the ground — because it's rarely just about the credits. Carbon is a signal. When it rises in your soil, it tells you something real is changing — water is being held longer, microbial life is recovering, nutrients are cycling more efficiently. Pasture responds better. Carrying capacity improves. The land starts doing more of the work. These aren't side effects of a carbon project — they're the reason the most experienced farmers we work with tell us the practice change was worth it regardless of the credit income. The credit is how we measure and reward that progress. Through our HORIZON platform, that measurement happens annually — meaning you're not waiting five years to see a return. You're tracking your soil, earning on your improvement, and building a clearer picture of how your country is performing over time. Productivity. Profitability. Long-term resilience. In our experience, when carbon is managed well, all three tend to move together. I'd genuinely enjoy walking you through what this could look like on your property. Would you be open to a sending through your lot and plan numbers so I can get a tailorered HORIZON snapshot report to see if it stacks up for your operation? engagements.body: Hi Scott, I hope you had a good weekend. Sorry we kept missing each other. We have a specialist grazier on the road with us, Hobbs Magaret, currently visiting producers across the Riverina who are doing interesting things on their country. Better pasture results, smarter grazing, stronger ground cover — the kind of results paid for in early mornings and tough seasons. I'd love to arrange for Hobbs to come out your way for a short visit either Thursday or Friday next week — an hour at most, entirely on your terms. There's no pitch involved. engagements.subject: Riverina soils might be worth more than you think
engagements.body: G'Day Brandon, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural "carbon sink" where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years. Why This Matters for Carbon: The combination of your soil types, pH management and yearly rainfall combination generate a significant carbon opportunity If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat?
